q: For warehouses, lakes and lakehouses, what should be defined before implementation?
options: The decision, grain, definitions, ownership and controls
why: A governed BI/data engineering solution begins with the decision and explicit operational/data definitions.

q: A one-to-many join is performed before aggregation. What risk must be checked?
options: Rows may multiply and inflate counts or sums
The database will always reject it
why: Join cardinality can multiply fact rows; validate grain and aggregate appropriately.

q: Which practice is essential for healthcare data security?
options: Put credentials in source code for convenience
Use least privilege, approved purpose and auditability
Share a public link for easy review
Assume a hidden report page protects data
why: Security requires controlled identity, permissions, data minimisation and monitoring.

q: What makes a data pipeline safely rerunnable?
options: Idempotent logic, stable keys and run metadata
why: Idempotency and controlled retries prevent duplicate or inconsistent side effects.

q: A successful refresh indicator proves that:
options: The source is complete and unbiased
The refresh operation reported success, but data quality still needs validation
why: Technical refresh success is distinct from data completeness, semantic correctness and clinical approval.

q: Which item belongs in a production handoff?
options: A runbook, metric definitions, tests, owners and access model
why: A supportable asset needs reproducibility, ownership, validation, access and operational documentation.
